prerequisites: Fundamentals of Quality Management and Statistics
Knowledge of basic methods and tools of Quality Management (Q7, M7 etc.)
Fundamentals of development methodology and manufacturing technology

learning_outcomes.text: Students can name and describe the appropriate methods of Quality Engineering for a quality-relevant task and provide examples for their application in the product development process.

Students conceptually structure the product development process in a quality-oriented manner by relating Quality Engineering methods and their results to each other and to the required engineering activities in development and production technology.
Students classify the importance of proactive quality management for manufacturing companies and justify the use of complex Quality Engineering methods in a utility-oriented way.
Students process practice-oriented complex tasks for integrated product and process development of socio-technical systems based on the module's knowledge and acquired skills.

Students consider the requirements of various stakeholders in product and process development in the sense of a holistic quality approach by systematically recording them using the learned methods, communicating development results, and involving stakeholders in validation.

Students can critically reflect on the importance of their engineering activity for quality in terms of customer satisfaction and recognize the benefit of scientifically based approaches in Quality Engineering. From this, they justify the use of complex methods in their professional environment.

syllabus_topics: Importance of proactive quality management - Zero-defect strategies
Product development phases - temporal and content classification of Quality Engineering in value creation processes - Quality advanced planning

Methodology from product development to manufacturing and assembly, e.g., Model Based Systems Engineering, Requirements Engineering, Quality Function Deployment QFD, Value Analysis VA, Failure Mode and Effect Analysis FMEA, Design of Experiments DOE, KVP concepts and strategies (e.g., Six Sigma)
assessment_rules: The graded examination performance is a written project report. The scope of the project report is approximately 10 - 20 pages per project group member.
